title: ടപ്പ് ടപ്പേന്ന് വെടിവെക്കും   Bombardier beetle #insects Sprays Acid From Its Rear #interestingfacts
description:
The video discusses unique beetles, particularly the Bombardier beetle, known for its ability to spray a chemical defense at predators. It explains the historical context of gunpowder, which was discovered by alchemists in China and is made from sulfur and potassium nitrate. The Carabidae family of beetles, including ground beetles, has evolved to have protective features and uses chemical defenses to deter predators. These beetles are carnivorous and help control pests in agriculture. Some species exhibit mimicry to avoid being eaten.
അന്തി പ്രിക്കി , വളി പൊട്ടൻ, തീപ്പാറ്റ , ഇലക്ട്രിക് പക്രു എന്നൊക്കെ ചില നാടുകളിൽ പേരുള്ളത് ബ്ലിസ്റ്റർ ബീറ്റിലിന് തന്നെയാണോ എന്നറിയില്ല. എന്റെ വക പേര്  പീരങ്കി വണ്ട് എന്നാണ്,  
ശത്രുവിനെ തുരത്താൻ തുരുതുരാ വെടിവെക്കാനുള്ള മരുന്നും ശരീരത്തിൽ സൂക്ഷിച്ച്  നടക്കുന്ന ചില വണ്ടുകളുണ്ട്. കരാബിഡെ വിഭാഗത്തിൽ പെട്ട  കുഞ്ഞ് നില വണ്ടുകളെ  ബൊംബാർഡിയർ ബീറ്റിലുകൾ (Bombardier beetle) എന്നാണ്  വിളിക്കുന്നത്- പീരങ്കി വണ്ടുകൾ! . അന്റാർട്ടിക്കിൽ ഒഴികെ ഭൂമിയിലെ കാടും മേടും ഉള്ള കരപ്രദേശങ്ങളിൽ പലയിടങ്ങളിലും ഇവരെ കാണാം.   അഞ്ഞൂറിൽ പരം സ്പീഷിസ് പീരങ്കി വണ്ടുകളെ ഇതുവരെയായി തിരിച്ചറിഞ്ഞിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഇരപിടിയന്മാരിൽ നിന്ന് പെട്ടന്ന് പറന്ന് പൊങ്ങി രക്ഷപ്പെടാൻ പറ്റാത്തവയാണ് ഇവർ.  ആരെങ്കിലും ഇവയെ ആക്രമിക്കാൻ വന്നാൽ, ഉള്ളിൽ പേടി കുടുങ്ങിയാലുടൻ  രക്ഷപ്പെടാനായി ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്ന തന്ത്രമാണ് പീരങ്കി വെടി.  പിങ്കാലുകളുടെ ഇടയിൽ വയറിന്` താഴെയുള്ള കുഞ്ഞ് കുഴലിലൂടെ ദിശതെറ്റാതെ ചറപറ വെടിയുതിർക്കും. വെടിക്ക് തീയില്ലാ എന്നു മാത്രം. പൊട്ടൽ  ശബ്ദവും, നീരാവിപ്പുകയുടെ അകമ്പടിയും ഒക്കെ ഉണ്ടാവും. രൂക്ഷഗന്ധമുള്ള വിഷപദാർത്ഥം , ഉന്നം തെറ്റാതെ ശത്രുവിന് നേരെ  ചീറ്റാൻ ഇതിന് കഴിയും. അഫ്രിക്കയിൽ കണ്ട് വരുന്ന ചില വണ്ടുകൾക്ക് 270 ഡിഗ്രി അളവിൽ    ചുറ്റുപാടും  വെടിവെയ്ക്കാനാവും. ‘ടപ്പേ’ എന്ന കുഞ്ഞ് ശബ്ദത്തോടെ പുകയോടെ തെറിക്കുന്ന  രാസദ്രാവകങ്ങൾക്ക് തിളക്കുന്നവെള്ളത്തിന്റെ അത്രയും ചൂടും ഉണ്ടാകും. ഇത്  ദേഹത്ത് വീണാൽ ശത്രുക്കൾ ജീവനും കൊണ്ട് ഓടും. ചിലന്തികളും വമ്പൻ ഉറുമ്പുകളും ചത്ത് പോകുകയും ചെയ്യും. 
Bombardier beetles are adephagan ground beetles (Carabidae) in the tribes Brachinini, Paussini, Ozaenini, or Metriini—more than 500 species altogether—which are most notable for the defense mechanism that gives them their name: when disturbed, they eject a hot noxious chemical spray from their pygidial glands with a popping sound.

There is a beetle that really shoots at those who attack it. Its name in English is Bombardier Beetle. That is why many people have given it these interesting Malayalam names. Anyway, we can only give it some respectable Malayalam name like Peerangi Vandu or Ketuvandu. In the 9th century, during the reign of Emperors of China, alchemists there accidentally discovered the chemical secret of making this gunpowder. They were trying to find medicines like the Elixir of Life or Amrit, a miracle medicine to defeat death. They also wanted to find chemical processes that could turn metals like iron into gold. That is why chemists in Arabia and China were experimenting with this for centuries. Many of the discoveries in our chemistry that we celebrate today were made by accident during their various experiments. One such discovery was the discovery of medicine. It was a mixture of six parts sulfur or sulfur and six parts potassium nitrate, a chemical substance that we still call gunpowder, along with the extracts of some plants in the Aristokia group. They used this type of gunpowder as a source of potassium nitrate. They relied heavily on the droppings of bats and sea birds for potassium nitrate. For thousands of years, the droppings of these bats had been deposited like rocks at the bottom of caves where bats had lived. As well as the droppings of sea birds, potassium nitrate was also collected and made from it. The first use of gunpowder discovered in this way was to launch rockets for celebrations and festivals. Competitions and celebrations were very common in China, and later they were used in cannons and guns to kill people and become a means of achieving great victories in wars. This knowledge slowly reached China through the Silk Route to many other parts through spies. The nature of wars, which used to be fought with spears and swords from close quarters, was changed completely with the use of cannons and guns. Later, we made gunpowder and powerful chemicals and reached missiles without missing a beat at long distances. But millions of years before humans evolved on Earth, they used this same strategy to chase away their enemies and prey. Bombardier beetles in the Carabid family are an amazing piece of knowledge. Today's video is about them. There are thousands of carabids in the Carabid family, that is, ground beetles, but they have evolved a pair of outer wings that are not used for flight, but are used as a shield, a strong shield, and they are called elytra. Therefore, They protect the inner wings by covering them. This electro-shield of many beetles is metallic, shiny, and many are black, which is why we call them black beetles. There are about 500 beetles in four categories of beetles in the genus of beetles that have evolved to be able to escape from enemies by spraying chemical sprays as a survival technique. Among them, beetles belonging to the genus Bracketness are very common and are very common. In India alone, there are about 65 species of beetles. Except for Antarctica, there are beetles in all forests and grasslands on earth. They are also abundant in our country. When an enemy comes to their senses, they spray a foul-smelling, burning, and smoking liquid from their backs to escape. They shoot at the enemy with great force, making a loud, hot, and smoke-filled sound. The small mammals, reptiles, insects, and spiders that come to eat them in the soil will then turn around in this shooting, like a bullet being fired at the street, and then this glowing chemical mixture will be shot out with a small sound, that is, it acts like a bomb being dropped on the street. They are called bombardier beetles because they bombard the street. In chemistry laboratories, when chemical mixtures taken from two test tubes are mixed into a third beaker, a large explosion, fire, and smoke occur. A similar event occurs inside them during this attack. Or, like the rocket propulsion combination chemical, this violent action is carried out by combining two hypergolic chemicals. For this, these beetles have a pair of glands at the tip of their abdomen. Each gland has two chambers, and the inner chamber of them is filled with hydroquinone and hydrogen peroxide solutions separately without mixing with each other. The outer chamber contains some Enzymes are proteins that act as catalysts for biochemical reactions. Enzymes are usually unable to fly away quickly when predators arrive. Therefore, these beetles have evolved this ability as an advantage to escape. When they are afraid of their enemies, they become trapped inside and are the last resort to escape if the attacker approaches. This cannonball is first fired by pressing the inner chambers and delivering hydrogen peroxide and hydroquinone to the chamber in front. The hydrogen peroxide, with the help of the catalyst enzyme layer in that chamber, decomposes into water and oxygen. The peroxidase enzymes in the chamber itself convert hydroquinone into paraquinone through oxidation. Since this is an exothermic chemical reaction, a lot of heat is produced as part of this chemical change. 204 Kilojoules per mole of heat energy are released when we put a cockroach in water. Similarly, as part of this chemical reaction, the heat energy released will raise the water content in the chamber to 100 degrees, meaning it will boil. The steam generated in this way will quickly increase the pressure in the chamber. The one-way valves to the body's internal cavities will close, and the boiling chemical compounds will return to the inside, protecting the internal parts of the cockroach from damage. The pressure will increase, and the outlet valve will suddenly blow out with a bang, like the valve of a pressure cooker. All of these actions take place in only a fraction of a second. Not only that, the one-fourth benzoquinone contained in the liquid that blows out is also a poison that is powerful enough to kill all its small enemies. It is enough to cause burning and stinging in the eyes of all the small creatures that are cockroaches, and to cause respiratory discomfort, 20 times in a row. They can store enough chemicals in both chambers to fire a single shot. They have a coating that prevents their internal parts from getting burned even when they are sprayed with such boiling substances. They also ignite the gunpowder in a gun and use its pressure to push the bullet out. In other words, they walk around with a gun that they make themselves with the bullet inside. They can turn their carabids in any direction they want through a small tube under their abdomen between their hind legs and shoot them without losing direction. They can shoot around some species of carabid beetles found in Africa up to 270 degrees. The only thing is that their shots do not fire, but the sound of the explosion and the accompanying steam make it look like a miniature set from a cowboy movie. These scenes are like those in a documentary introducing Richard Attambo or Bombardier Beetles, and there are also good sound effects when shooting like this. In fact, you can't hear a sound that is so terrible. Charles Darwin has already spoken about some of the pains experienced due to the intensity of the mixtures sprayed by the Carabid beetles. It is not enough to know the survival strategy of these beetles. You also need to get to know what their lives are like. The beetles of the Carabid family are carnivores that eat small insects. Although their main prey is in the soil, their larvae are also good predators. They are good at catching the larvae of hornworms and mole crickets, which cause great harm to our agriculture, and aphids. Therefore, they can be considered as an agricultural pest controller. In addition, their larvae have a special characteristic. They live as parasites on the bodies of other organisms. Not only do they live like that, they also kill them. The Carabid beetles mainly hunt for prey at night. During the day, they also have a habit of gathering in groups. These special characteristics of such beetles are the ability to shoot. Similarly, predators who know the ability to squirt corrosive fluids or those who have previous experience with them usually avoid them when they see them. Some species also have some marks on their bodies, such as bright colors, which is a warning to other predators that if you touch me, you will get caught. This is called aposomotism. Interestingly, some creatures use this as an opportunity to recognize that these beetles, which belong to the Carabid family, are not attacked by predators very quickly.
